question.worked_solution:
We will solve this problem using integration by parts. We start by defining $u$ and ${v}^{′},$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}u=\operatorname{ln}⁡x & \,⟹\,{u}^{′}=\frac{1}{x} \\ {v}^{′}=2{x}^{2} & \,⟹\,v=\int 2{x}^{2}\,dx=\frac{2{x}^{3}}{3}\end{aligned}
$$

Using the formula of integration by parts, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{1}^{{e}^{2}}2{x}^{2}\operatorname{ln}⁡(x)\,\text{d}x & ={\int }_{1}^{{e}^{2}}u{v}^{′}\,\text{d}x \\  & =uv{|}_{1}^{{e}^{2}}-{\int }_{1}^{{e}^{2}}v{u}^{′}\,\text{d}x \\  & =\operatorname{ln}⁡x(\frac{2{x}^{3}}{3}){|}_{1}^{{e}^{2}}-{\int }_{1}^{{e}^{2}}(\frac{2{x}^{3}}{3})(\frac{1}{x})\,\text{d}x \\  & =[\frac{2({e}^{2})^{3}\operatorname{ln}⁡({e}^{2})}{3}-\frac{2(1)^{3}\operatorname{ln}⁡(1)}{3}]-\frac{2}{3}{\int }_{1}^{{e}^{2}}{x}^{2}\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{2{e}^{6}\operatorname{ln}⁡({e}^{2})}{3}-\frac{2{x}^{3}}{9}{|}_{1}^{{e}^{2}} \\  & =\frac{4{e}^{6}}{3}-(\frac{2{e}^{6}}{9}-\frac{2}{9}) \\  & =\frac{1}{9}(12{e}^{6}-2{e}^{6}+2) \\  & =\frac{2}{9}(5{e}^{6}+1).\end{aligned}
$$
